stories.title: The Plan: Extell’s 70-Unit 50 West 66th Street Leans Into Luxury Via Hospitality
stories.excerpt: Central Park views? Check. An abundance of natural light? Check. Doorman? Check. Resort-quality amenities? Check. Honestly, once you move in there’s really no reason to ever leave Extell’s 50 West 66th Street. The 70-story condominium building has two sides: the house, which has 84 units, and the tower with 37 units. Residents began moving in last year, but the building is still undergoing some finishing touches and has a few units that need to be completed. Still, Janice Chang of Douglas Elliman said most buyers purchased based solely on the renderings and floor plans, as they were so taken with the possibilities. “We’ve sold a lot of these apartments sight unseen,” Chang said. “We just started showing people the furnished models, and it’s been so well received, it’s so incredible.” The view from the tower units is nothing short of spectacular. Any of these homes — which range in size from two to six bedrooms and in price from $8 million to $85 million — would make for the perfect retreat for a snuggly day at home reading and watching the city’s activity go by. “This is the best view because it’s panoramic,” Chang said while showing Commercial Observer around a recently completed, nearly 10,000-square-foot unit. “It’s a sweep from the Hudson River all the way to Central Park South. And you’re not very high, you can see all of the trees and landmarks, and up to the George Washington Bridge.” There are touches of luxury throughout each unit, including the white marble kitchens with Miele appliances, double ovens and wine refrigerators. There’s also cabinetry by designer SmallBone, and bathrooms with heated floors, rain showers and deep-soaking tubs. (You know CO is a sucker for a good tub.) There are uniquely designed light fixtures in the units and throughout the building, almost like statement pieces in their own right, bringing more sophistication to the property. “After people move in, they tell me they love it. bullets: Extell's 50 West 66th Street: 121 total units ($8M–$85M), 70-story mixed condo tower in Manhattan.
Buyers purchasing sight-unseen based on renderings; furnished models now showing strong reception.
Hospitality-grade amenities and services positioning product as ultra-luxury alternative to traditional housing.
stories.summary: Extell's 50 West 66th Street in Manhattan—121 condos across a 70-story building with unit prices ranging $8M to $85M—is leaning into hospitality-grade service and amenities to differentiate its luxury product. Residents have begun moving in, though units are still completing. Most buyers committed based on renderings and floor plans alone, and the newly furnished models are generating strong market reception.
stories.impact: This signals a sustained ultra-luxury condo market in Manhattan's prime locations, but the hospitality service model and high entry price ($8M floor) address a narrow demand slice and don't directly inform multifamily rental supply or demand dynamics that drive TCR's core underwriting and development pipeline.

stories.title: Looking Past the Noise: A More Nuanced View of Multifamily
stories.excerpt: The multifamily market is entering a new phase defined less by broad national narratives and more by local realities, operational discipline, and selective opportunity. In a recent conversation on “Inside the Deal, a CRE Podcast by Berkadia®,” host Ernie Katai, executive vice president – head of production for Berkadia, sat down with rental housing economist Jay Parsons to unpack what is actually happening across multifamily today — beyond the noise of headlines and broad-brush narratives. Parsons emphasized that many common multifamily narratives are too simplistic. He noted that rental housing tends to perform best when the broader economy is strong, household formation is healthy, and consumer confidence is rising, underscoring how closely multifamily is tied to the overall state of the economy. If there is one word Parsons uses repeatedly, it is “resilient.” He described today’s apartment market as choppy and renter-favorable, but still remarkably durable. Even after the largest supply wave since the 1970s, national rent declines have remained relatively modest in aggregate, and vacancy has not deteriorated as severely as many feared. Likewise, while valuations are down from peak levels, the worst-case distress scenarios that many expected several years ago have not materialized at scale. Instead, debt availability and recapitalization have allowed many owners to hold on longer than expected, softening what could have been a far more dramatic correction. That does not mean conditions are easy. Parsons characterized the current phase as both a messy transition and a recovery — a “two steps forward, one step back” environment. Deals are getting done, but not without obstacles. bullets: Berkadia economist: multifamily market is choppy and renter-favorable but 'resilient' post-supply wave.
National rent declines modest despite largest supply since 1970s; vacancy worse than feared but manageable.
Thesis: market performance tied to broad economy, household formation, consumer confidence—not monolithic narratives.
stories.summary: Berkadia and economist Jay Parsons argue the multifamily market is entering a phase where local realities, not broad headlines, drive outcomes. Despite the largest supply wave since the 1970s, national rent declines have remained modest, and vacancy deterioration is less severe than feared. Parsons emphasizes that apartment performance depends on macro factors—strong economy, healthy household formation, rising consumer confidence—making the market resilient but market-and-submarket-specific.
stories.impact: This reframes TCR's underwriting discipline: oversimplified 'multifamily is saturated' narratives are losing currency, but it reinforces the critical importance of market-by-market and submarket-level selection, household formation tracking, and macro sensitivity. Developers with conviction on local demand and operational discipline will find pockets of opportunity where supply headwinds are less acute and renter absorption is stronger.

stories.title: Law Firm Dunn Isaacson Rhee Establishes NYC Office at 7 World Trade Center
stories.excerpt: Silverstein Properties announced that Dunn Isaacson Rhee LLP has signed a new lease for 11,167 square feet of office space on the 34th floor of 7 World Trade Center. The lease establishes a New York office for the firm, an elite litigation boutique.“Dunn Isaacson Rhee represents the caliber of organization that continues to define 7 World Trade Center as one of Downtown Manhattan’s premier office destinations,” said Keith Cody, Head of Commercial Leasing at Silverstein Properties. “Today’s leading firms are seeking workplaces that reflect their brand, support their people, and provide an exceptional experience for their clients. Through thoughtful design, hospitality-driven amenities, and a commitment to excellence, 7 World Trade Center continues to deliver an environment that meets those expectations.”Tenant representation was provided by Lisa Ann Pollakowski, Cory Gahr and Richard Plehn of Lee & Associates. Ownership was represented in-house by Cody, Gordon Hough, and Harlan Strader, with CBRE agency leasing support from MaryAnn Tighe and team. The post Law Firm Dunn Isaacson Rhee Establishes NYC Office at 7 World Trade Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Dunn Isaacson Rhee LLP leases 11,167 SF at 7 World Trade Center, downtown Manhattan office.
Elite litigation boutique establishing first NYC office; signals office demand for quality brand spaces.
Silverstein positioning 7 WTC as premier destination for high-caliber firms seeking branded workplaces.
stories.summary: Silverstein Properties announced that litigation boutique Dunn Isaacson Rhee LLP has leased 11,167 square feet on the 34th floor of 7 World Trade Center in downtown Manhattan. The firm is establishing its first New York office at this premier address, signaling selective office tenant demand in Lower Manhattan for high-quality branded spaces.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. Office leasing in lower Manhattan is upstream from rental housing demand—strong office market does support white-collar job growth and worker population, but this single boutique lease is not a demand signal material enough for TCR's acquisition and development planning.

stories.title: Newmark Closes Note Sale on San Pedro Adaptive Reuse
stories.excerpt: Newmark arranged the sale of a note secured by Topaz Tower, a fully entitled adaptive reuse development project located at 222 W. 6th St. in San Pedro. The 12-story, 309,732-square-foot office tower is entitled for conversion to 246 market-rate multifamily units. Executive managing director Ryan Plummer, co-head of U.S. Capital Markets Kevin Shannon, vice chairman Ken White, senior managing director Chris Benton and managing director Anthony Muhlstein represented the lender. The buyer was 222 PV Harbor View, LLC, a private Los Angeles-based residential developer. “Topaz Tower represents an exceptionally rare opportunity to acquire a fully entitled coastal high-rise multifamily conversion with scale, ocean views and an immediate execution path in a rapidly evolving submarket,” said Plummer. Topaz Tower Apartments will include a mix of studio, one-, two- and three-bedroom residences with an average unit size of 835 square feet. Planned amenities include a rooftop deck with a resort-style pool, ocean-view units, balconies and high ceilings. Stay ahead of the multifamily market at Connect Apartments. bullets: Topaz Tower (222 W. 6th St., San Pedro): 12-story office tower fully entitled for 246 market-rate apartments.
Newmark closed note sale to 222 PV Harbor View LLC, private LA developer; adaptive reuse with ocean views.
Mix of studio–3BR units (835 SF avg), rooftop pool, balconies; immediate execution path in evolving submarket.
stories.summary: Newmark closed a note sale on Topaz Tower, a fully entitled 12-story adaptive reuse development in San Pedro, California, converting office to 246 market-rate multifamily units. Buyer 222 PV Harbor View LLC, a Los Angeles-based residential developer, acquired the asset which includes studio through 3-bedroom units averaging 835 SF, with ocean views and resort-style amenities. The property has clear entitlements and execution path.
stories.impact: San Pedro (coastal LA submarket) is experiencing infill and redevelopment momentum. This entitled office-to-multifamily conversion signals: (1) office stock repositioning as capital-efficient housing supply in transit-adjacent coastal markets, (2) acquisition window for entitled conversion projects where regulatory/entitlement risk is absorbed, and (3) viable demand for coastal high-rise rental product with scale and ocean exposure. TCR should scout similar fully entitled conversion opportunities in LA's secondary coastal corridors before competing developers lock supply.

stories.title: Venture X Coworking Location to Open in Pompano Beach
stories.excerpt: Priddy Spaces has signed a 20,000-square-foot lease for a Venture X coworking location in Pompano Beach, Fla. The coworking operator signed a 10-year lease at a 44,102-square-foot office property within Grover Corlew’s Mayla Pompano mixed-use development. Located at 2335 East Atlantic Boulevard, the four-story office building sits two blocks east of Dixie Highway and was constructed in 2020. The coworking outpost — which will span the building’s second, third and fourth floors — will feature 85 private office suites and four meeting rooms. It’s expected to open next year. “Pompano Beach is experiencing one of the most exciting transformations in South Florida,” Kevin Priddy, co-founder and CEO of Priddy Spaces, said in a statement. “The combination of new residential development, improved infrastructure, vibrant dining and retail, and its proximity to the beach has created an environment where businesses and talent want to be.” Pompano Beach, long a working-class town, is seeing a rush of luxury condo development along its coast, from the likes of Miami-based Related Group and other developers. West Palm Beach-based Priddy Spaces is a franchisee of Venture X, operating five locations in South Florida, with Vast Coworking Group serving as the franchisor. Private equity firm New State Capital Partners purchased Vast Coworking Group earlier this year for an undisclosed amount. Priddy Spaces operates a Venture X location in nearby Boca Raton at Grover Corlew’s Palmetto Central office campus. The four-acre Mayla Pompano mixed-use development includes a 355-unit apartment building and two other office properties. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Venture X coworking lease: 20,000 SF across 44,102 SF office building in Pompano Beach, Fla., 10-year term.
Space spans 2nd–4th floors of 2020-built office; 85 private suites, 4 meeting rooms; opens 2025.
Pompano Beach undergoing 'one of most exciting transformations in South Florida'—luxury condos, dining, retail, infrastructure.
stories.summary: Priddy Spaces signed a 10-year lease for a Venture X coworking location in Pompano Beach, Florida, occupying 20,000 square feet (floors 2–4) of a 44,102 SF office building within Grover Corlew's Mayla Pompano mixed-use development. The location will feature 85 private office suites and four meeting rooms, opening in 2025. Leadership cited Pompano's transformation—new residential, infrastructure, dining, retail—as driver.
stories.impact: Pompano Beach, historically working-class, is pivoting to luxury residential and mixed-use infill (Related Group and others building condos). Coworking anchor signals talent/entrepreneurial density clustering in the market. This creates positive demand tailwinds for multifamily in Pompano: job growth, young professional migration, lifestyle amenities maturity. TCR should evaluate rental development sites in walkable Pompano corridors within 0.5 miles of dining/retail/beach access; this demographic is renter-friendly and upscale.

stories.title: Domain Lines Up $176M Financing for Mixed-Income Astoria Rentals
stories.excerpt: The Domain Companies has closed on $175.6 million in financing with Wells Fargo for a new mixed-income housing project called Elara, which will deliver 429 new apartments in Astoria, Queens. Domain’s equity partners on the deal are Canyon Partners Real Estate and BLDG Management. The financing was brokered by Chris Peck and Nicco Lupo of JLL Capital Markets.  “Astoria is one of New York’s most vibrant and culturally rich neighborhoods, and it has long held a special place in Domain’s history,” said Matt Schwartz, co-CEO of Domain Companies.“We’re proud to deepen that connection by delivering a thoughtfully designed residential community that reflects the character of the neighborhood while offering one of the highest-quality living experiences in the market.” The project includes an 18-story building with 330 apartments called Elara East, and a 12-story building with 99 apartments named Elara West. The development includes 107 permanently affordable homes. The buildings are located at 35-45, 35-33 and 35-42 41st St., with Elara West anticipated to open in February 2028, and Elara East expected in September 2028. bullets: Domain Companies closes $175.6M Wells Fargo financing for Elara (429 apartments) in Astoria, Queens.
Two buildings: Elara East (18-story, 330 units) opening Sept 2028; Elara West (12-story, 99 units) opening Feb 2028.

stories.summary: The Domain Companies closed $175.6 million in financing with Wells Fargo for Elara, a mixed-income rental project delivering 429 apartments across two buildings in Astoria, Queens. Elara East (18-story, 330 units, opening Sept 2028) and Elara West (12-story, 99 units, opening Feb 2028) will include 107 permanently affordable homes. Equity partners are Canyon Partners Real Estate and BLDG Management.
stories.impact: Astoria continues to attract institutional capital and major development despite Queens market saturation concerns. The ability to close $176M for a 429-unit mixed-income project signals: (1) permanent affordability mandates remain financeable (likely via tax credits and subsidy), (2) Queens rental demand remains sufficient to support mid-market + affordable blend, (3) development timeline extends 3+ years, requiring TCR to model absorption against competing Queens supply. Astoria submarkets with lower density zoning and less pipeline may offer better IRR opportunities.

stories.title: La La Land Cafe Signs with Brixton Capital for First San Diego Location
stories.excerpt: Brixton Capital, a vertically integrated owner and operator of retail and multifamily properties, has secured a lease with La La Land Café to occupy the mezzanine terrace and café space at its upscale Del Mar Plaza retail destination. La La Land will occupy 1,168 square feet of interior space, with additional sitting and queueing space extending onto the terrace deck. The construction start and grand opening dates are not yet determined. The space was formerly occupied by Pacifica Breeze Café. “We’re proud to be first-to-market attracting a dynamic brand that has grown to over 30 locations since its founding in 2019,” said Brixton Capital founder and chairman Marc Brutten. “We expect the grand opening will be very well attended, and that La La Land Café at Del Mar Plaza will remain a very popular social destination.” Victoria Pappas, Brittney Austin and Linda Rubiola of SHOP Companies represented La La Land, while Brixton Capital represented itself, with support from Andrew Shemirani and Ashley Tiefel at Urban Property Group. Lease terms were not disclosed. The post La La Land Cafe Signs with Brixton Capital for First San Diego Location appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: La La Land Café (30+ locations, founded 2019) signs first San Diego location at Brixton Capital's Del Mar Plaza.
1,168 SF interior + terrace space; replaces Pacifica Breeze Café; opening timeline TBD.
Brixton Capital positioning Del Mar Plaza as upscale retail destination with dynamic F&B anchors.
stories.summary: Brixton Capital secured a lease with La La Land Café for 1,168 square feet at Del Mar Plaza in San Diego, marking La La Land's first location in the market. The fast-growing brand (30+ locations since 2019) will occupy interior space plus terrace, replacing the former Pacifica Breeze Café. Grand opening date not yet determined; lease terms undisclosed.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. This is F&B retail leasing in an upscale shopping center. However, La La Land's rapid expansion and strong early-market selection suggest a national lifestyle/social venue brand capturing affluent, younger demographics—a positive indicator for premium residential markets where TCR develops. No specific supply or demand signal for rental housing.

stories.title: JLL Arranges Sale of Two Twin Cities Seniors Housing Properties
stories.excerpt: JLL has arranged the sale of Boulder Ponds Senior Living and Round Lake Senior Living, a 216-unit portfolio of seniors housing communities located in Lake Elmo and Arden Hills, Minnesota. JLL’s Seniors Housing Capital Markets team represented the seller, Trident Development, in the transaction and secured the buyer, LTC Properties, Inc. Lifespark will remain the operator of both communities. Developed by Trident Development, the portfolio comprises two purpose-built communities strategically located within the Twin Cities submarkets. Both communities offer independent living, assisted living and memory care services. Boulder Ponds Senior Living, completed in 2020, is a 95-unit community in Lake Elmo located at 192 Jade Trail N. The property has demonstrated strong operating performance and stability, maintaining approximately 98% occupancy. Round Lake Senior Living, which opened in 2023, is a 121-unit community in Arden Hills at 1740 Parkshore Dr. The community benefits from convenient access to major employment centers, retail amenities and healthcare services. The post JLL Arranges Sale of Two Twin Cities Seniors Housing Properties appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: JLL arranges sale of Boulder Ponds (95 units, Lake Elmo) and Round Lake (121 units, Arden Hills) senior living.
Portfolio: 216-unit seniors housing; 98% occupancy at Boulder Ponds (opened 2020); Round Lake opened 2023.
Buyer: LTC Properties, Inc.; operator remains Lifespark; Twin Cities stronghold for purpose-built seniors communities.
stories.summary: JLL facilitated the sale of two purpose-built seniors housing communities in the Twin Cities—Boulder Ponds Senior Living (95 units, Lake Elmo, opened 2020, ~98% occupied) and Round Lake Senior Living (121 units, Arden Hills, opened 2023)—to LTC Properties, Inc. Portfolio total: 216 units. Lifespark continues to operate both communities, which offer independent living, assisted living, and memory care.
stories.impact: Senior housing is a distinct asset class from TCR's core multifamily rental development, with different financing, ops, and exit profiles. However, strong occupancy at newer communities (98% at Boulder Ponds; recent stabilization at Round Lake) and rapid portfolio sale to established operator (LTC) signals healthy seniors housing demand in Twin Cities, particularly in suburban markets with healthcare access. Not actionable for TCR unless pursuing seniors or co-living product.

stories.title: AI Wealth Management Platform Vise Grabs 12K SF at 50 Ninth Avenue
stories.excerpt: Artificial intelligence-powered wealth management platform Vise is moving from SoHo to 50 Ninth Avenue in the Meatpacking District, where it will quadruple its office space to 11,949 square feet. The space spans the second floor of several combined historic townhomes along the Ninth Avenue frontage and therefore has dramatic, over 20 foot-high pitched ceilings and an atrium outdoor garden. Rob Kluge and Brandon Charnas of Current Real Estate Advisors represented the tenant in the 10-year lease. Howard Hersch, Greg Conen, Jennifer Schreiber and Natalie Serio of Newmark represented the building owner, Tavros Capital, which will build out the space. The asking rent was $150 per square foot. Vise is an AI-driven wealth management platform for independent advisors founded by Samir Vasavada and Runik Mehrotra that launched in November 2019. It hosts over $100 billion in assets and the firm is reported to be valued at over $22 billion. It is currently located in 4,000 square feet of office space at 521 Broadway in SoHo. In searching for new digs, Vise was focused on upgrading both its office and culture. “We worked with ownership on a creative solution whereby the ground-floor retailer, Jen Rubio’s fashion company — now known as Elsa, which was then negotiating their deal — would expand upstairs and take roughly another 4,000 to 5,000 square feet on the West 14th Street side of the floor,” Charnas said. “That allowed us to create a space for Vise that fit both their program and their budget.” “We worked through multiple iterations with ownership and the architect to take what had been one larger floor and create the right long-term home for Vise,” added Kluge. The resulting space primarily overlooks Ninth Avenue and sits directly across from the Apple store, with dramatic vaulted ceilings, tons of light and a build-out being designed specifically around Vise’s needs and specifications. It will also sit above the new Delilah club and across from the planned Annabel’s member
bullets: Vise (AI wealth mgmt, $22B valuation, $100B+ AUM) quadruples office space to 11,949 SF at 50 Ninth Avenue, Meatpacking.
10-year lease at $150/SF; expands from 4,000 SF SoHo space; dramatic 20+ ft ceilings, garden atrium.
Founded Nov 2019; high-growth fintech firm anchoring premium Manhattan office market with modern amenities.
stories.summary: AI-powered wealth management platform Vise is relocating from SoHo to 50 Ninth Avenue in Manhattan's Meatpacking District, quadrupling its office footprint to 11,949 square feet on a 10-year lease at $150/SF. The space features dramatic 20-foot-plus ceilings and an atrium garden. Vise, valued at $22 billion and hosting $100 billion in AUM, represents high-growth fintech anchoring premium Manhattan office.
stories.impact: Another Manhattan office lease for a high-growth, VC-backed tech/fintech firm. While office demand is outside TCR's core, this signals continued concentration of well-capitalized, young-demographic talent and employers in Manhattan (especially West Village/Meatpacking), supporting rental demand for proximate multifamily. No direct supply or capital implication for TCR development.

stories.title: SME Capital Forced to Hand Over Hudson Yards Condo Building to Residents
stories.excerpt: Private investment firm SME Capital Ventures is handing ownership of 441 West 37th Street to the condominium board after an investigation by the New York Attorney General’s office. SME acquired the building out of foreclosure in 2023. It then failed to pay bills related to the Hudson Yards property and neglected safety violations, leading to a settlement to pay $700,000, according to Attorney General Letitia James. Built in 2020 by Levi Balkany, the nine-unit building went into foreclosure in 2023. SME never reported to the state that it was the winning bidder in the auction and never acknowledged that it owned the building, leaving residents to pick up the tab for things like a new $15,824 certificate of occupancy, according to the AG. Some of the units were rented out while awaiting buyers, including 35 formerly homeless people who were ousted around the time SME took control of the building, according to The Real Deal. “Private equity firms do not get to pick and choose which laws apply to them,” James said in a statement. “When this company took control of a Manhattan condo building, it took on real legal responsibilities to the homeowners who lived there. For two years, SME Capital dodged those duties while still collecting rent checks. My office will keep holding these firms accountable when they put profits over New Yorkers’ safety.” Balkany could not be reached for comment. SME’s Eran Silverberg signed the settlement agreement, but the firm’s attorney Ken Breen attested that the building’s problems all boil down to developer failing in his own responsibilities to the residents of the building, leaving SME to “inherited a building that had been left in regulatory limbo.” “We chose to resolve this matter because the homeowners at 441 West 37th Street had already suffered enough as a result of Mr. Balkany’s conduct,” Breen said in a statement. “Under the terms of the settlement, SME C
bullets: SME Capital Ventures forced to hand over 441 W. 37th St. (9-unit condo) to residents by NY AG office.
SME acquired building out of foreclosure in 2023, failed to pay bills, violated safety codes; settled for $700K.
Building built 2020 by Levi Balkany; 35 homeless residents ousted when SME took control; AG enforcement action.
stories.summary: The New York Attorney General's office compelled SME Capital Ventures to hand over ownership of 441 West 37th Street (Hudson Yards, 9-unit condo) to the condominium board after investigation revealed SME—which acquired the building at foreclosure auction in 2023—failed to pay operating expenses, violated safety codes, and ousted 35 formerly homeless residents. SME settled by paying $700,000 and surrendering title.
stories.impact: This is enforcement action on a failed foreclosure play in condo conversion, not a multifamily rental signal. However, it flags regulatory and reputational risk for developers acquiring distressed/foreclosed buildings in Manhattan without robust due diligence on tenant protections and legal compliance. For TCR: avoid aggressive foreclosure or distressed condo plays in NYC without strong legal, tax, and title review; regulatory scrutiny on affordable/vulnerable tenant displacement is intensifying.
